root_cause.text: The function `omap_crypto_copy_sg_lists()` used `sizeof(*sg)` (size of a pointer) instead of `sizeof(*new_sg)` (size of a `struct scatterlist`) when allocating memory for the scatterlist array, causing a heap buffer overflow due to undersized allocation.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the allocation from `kmalloc_array(n, sizeof(*sg), GFP_KERNEL)` to `kmalloc_array(n, sizeof(*new_sg), GFP_KERNEL)`. The commit message explicitly states: "was allocating an array of scatterlist pointers, not scatterlist objects, resulting in a 4x too small allocation." This mismatch leads to writing scatterlist objects into a buffer intended for pointers, causing out-of-bounds writes.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function omap_crypto_copy_sg_lists() allocates memory using 'kmalloc_array(n, sizeof(*sg), GFP_KERNEL)'. Here, 'sizeof(*sg)' is the size of a pointer (struct scatterlist *), not the size of a struct scatterlist. This undersized allocation will cause a heap buffer overflow when the code later accesses elements of 'new_sg' as struct scatterlist. The fix would be to use 'sizeof(*new_sg)' or 'sizeof(struct scatterlist)'. Since this commit introduces the vulnerable code, has_bug is true and is_fixed is false.
